_readme: Editable reference mapping ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls to Airlock Digital policy configuration. Edit descriptions, add/remove controls, or tune rule thresholds per client engagement. Controls with rule type 'manual' are not yet backed by a confirmed Airlock field and will show as 'unknown' in reports until a real rule is defined.

controls.title: A.8.7
controls.name: Protection against malware
controls.description: Detection, prevention, and recovery controls against malware. Application allowlisting combined with active blocklisting of known-bad software provides layered evidence for this control.

controls.title: A.8.8
controls.name: Management of technical vulnerabilities
controls.description: MANUAL — not yet backed by a confirmed Airlock field. Needs input on what signal(s) in the policy response (if any) indicate vulnerability-management posture, e.g. hash database currency, or targeted blocking of known-vulnerable software.

controls.title: A.8.9
controls.name: Configuration management
controls.description: DRAFT — please confirm. Currently checks only whether the group avoids ad hoc trust overrides (trusted_config) that bypass the normal managed policy. This is a narrow proxy, not a full configuration-management assessment — open to a better signal if one exists.

controls.title: A.8.12
controls.name: Data leakage prevention
controls.description: MANUAL — not yet backed by a confirmed Airlock field. Needs input on what signal(s) in the policy response (if any) map to DLP, since this isn't obviously covered by core application allowlisting.

controls.title: A.8.15
controls.name: Logging
controls.description: MANUAL — not yet backed by a confirmed Airlock field. Needs input on which field (if any) reflects whether execution logging is actually enabled/active for a group, versus just notification settings.

controls.title: A.8.19
controls.name: Installation of software on operational systems
controls.description: Restricting what software can be installed and executed on operational systems. Airlock's core application allowlisting capability maps directly to this control: a group actively enforcing (not just auditing) is providing real preventive evidence, not just visibility.
